Subject: Hosted API cost qualification + peak TPS follow-up

Hi Julie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few follow-ups so we can land a crisp hosted quote: 

Recap of what you shared today:
- Primary use: in-app clinical summarization + patient Q&A for the nursing workstation.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~40M total tokens / month (combined prompts + completions).
- Peak characteristics: sustained peaks of ~10–12 TPS during morning rounds; short bursts to ~18 TPS during audit windows.
- Quality: need >= 95% availability SLA and deterministic latency under 350ms p95 for short prompts.

Questions / asks for confirmation (so we can price accurately):
1) Can you reconfirm expected monthly token range (you mentioned 30–50M, is 40M a good central estimate?)
2) Are you planning to commit to a monthly token minimum or prefer pay-as-you-go with overage?
3) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of <$150 per 1M tokens on peak usage — is that the target for effective blended price or a hard ceiling?
4) Any procurement timelines or PO terms we should be aware of (Net 30/45, SOW, insurance limits)?

Attached is a lightweight estimate workbook with two pricing scenarios (pay-as-you-go vs. 12-month commit) and a ratecard for hosted API. I call out an initial committed band that would get you close to the cost target once we account for caching and prefix reuse.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to the questions above by EOD Friday 2/13.
- I’ll prepare a calibrated quote (including burst allowance and an SLA addendum) for your procurement team.
- Optional: 30-minute ops deep-dive to validate request size distribution and token split (prompt vs. completion).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the recap and the file. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Steady-state: 40M tokens/month is our best estimate for Q3. We expect a +/- 20% variance depending on adoption.
- Peaks: 10–12 TPS is typical during clinician shift overlaps; we have scheduled events (quarterly audits) that can create 15–18 TPS bursts lasting ~10–30 minutes.
- Commitment: Procurement prefers to start with a 3-month pilot (pay-as-you-go) and move to a 12-month committed band if latency and unit economics meet our expectations.
- Budget: loosely allocated $12k–$18k/month for this service initially. Our engineering VP asked if you can get us to a blended $/1M tokens that is <= $150 — that’s our target threshold to move from pilot to commit.

Procurement notes: standard terms; likely Net30. We’ll share a pre-approved PO template if we proceed.

Two quick questions for you: 1) if we run pay-as-you-go at 40M tokens, what would the expected monthly bill look like (ballpark)? 2) what burst policy do you include for hosted customers — do short 20% overages get absorbed or billed immediately?

Appreciate it — Julie
Julie Park
Director, Product Operations | Acme Health
julie.park@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-2246

Subject: Re: Hosted API cost qualification + peak TPS follow-up

Hi Julie —

Thanks — super helpful. Quick answers and a proposed commercial path: 

1) Ballpark for pay-as-you-go at ~40M tokens/mo
- List hosted rate: $220 per 1M tokens => ~ $8,800/month at 40M.
- With typical runtime optimizations (prefix caching, request batching, rate-limited output) we often see an effective reduction of ~20–30% for in-app workloads like yours; that brings an expected range of $6,000–$7,500/month for pay-as-you-go (variable).

2) Burst policy
- Hosted customers get an automatic short-burst buffer (roughly 25% of committed TPS) before we throttle or apply explicit burst billing. Short bursts (<=30 min) are absorbed without separate charges if average daily usage stays within 120% of baseline. For sustained overages we bill at the overage rate in the ratecard. We’ll include concrete burst SLA language in the quote.

3) To reach your target <= $150 / 1M tokens (blended) we recommend:
- 12-month commit at 40M/mo or a stepped commit (3mo pilot -> convert to commit) with pricing at $140 / 1M tokens effective after commit and a 3% monthly overage allowance.
- Additional operational levers: per-route caching (reduces completion tokens), lower-precision quantized model variants for lower-cost bulk operations, and request coalescing at the SDK level.

Proposed next step: I’ll produce a two-option quote: A) 3-month pilot (PAYG) with burst absorb policy and sample estimate; B) 12-month commit at $140 / 1M (with SLA and 20% discount on enterprise support). I’ll route the contract to procurement once you pick a path.

I’ve attached the ratecard PDF and updated the workbook to show both scenarios. If accepted, Ben (cc’d) can weigh in on one-time onboarding/training credits. Can you confirm whether Acme needs SOC2 evidence and your security questionnaire returned during the pilot?

Best,
Soojin
